errors.description: The stated off-diagonal identity is missing the exclusion of k=i (equivalently, division by c_j-c_i). It contradicts the identity obtained in the proof.
errors.evidence: The lemma gives the product over k≠j, whereas its proof gives the product over k≠i,j. For n=1, c_0=0, c_1=2, i=0, j=1, the left side is the derivative of ψ(x)=x-2, namely 1, but the stated right side is 2.

errors.location: Equation (2.9), the subsequent binomial-coefficient claim, and Theorem 2.2
errors.description: The definition of the generalized coefficient at c_0 has an erroneous sign for odd n. Consequently, the second off-diagonal expression in Theorem 2.2 disagrees with its first expression when an index is zero.
errors.evidence: For c_i=i, (2.9) gives binom(c_n,c_0)=(-1)^n, although the manuscript claims it equals binom(n,0)=1. With n=1, c_0=0, c_1=1, Theorem 2.2's product expression gives W_01=-1, but its generalized-binomial expression gives W_01=+1.

errors.location: Introduction, identification of the BIM inverse with W_n^T; Section 2.2, formula for N
errors.description: The assertion that the BIM inverse is exactly W_n^T for equidistant nodes conflicts with the manuscript's explicit BIM inverse N.
errors.evidence: The introduction states that the BIM inverse is 'exactly W_n^T' for c_i=i. Section 2.2 instead gives N=D_n(V_n D_n V_n^{-1}D_n^{-1})D_n^{-1}+D_n^{-1}. For n=1 and c_0=0, c_1=1, the formulas give W_n^T=[1] and N=[2], so these cannot be the same inverse.

errors.location: Section 4.2, equation (4.2) and the discussion of Example 4
errors.description: Equidistant nodes can produce complete cancellation and exactly zero diagonal entries. The claim that heavy cancellation does not occur is false, and the stated componentwise relative-error metric is undefined at those entries without a zero-denominator convention.
errors.evidence: For c_k=k and n=2m, Corollary 2.3 gives W_mm=∑_{p=1}^m 1/p−∑_{p=1}^m 1/p=0, while the sum of absolute reciprocal terms is 2∑_{p=1}^m 1/p>0. Section 4.2 says 'heavy cancellation does not occur in the sum', and Err_2 in (4.2) divides by |W^q_ij| for every entry while treating W^q as exact; the central diagonal therefore has a zero denominator.
